dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: Ah yeah... Now that I think about it, that should've looked like that, no...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Selling any books around here?

dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: Oh, they're all here. Feel free to browse.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like what?

dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, uh, I was thinking about the rift valley in Novokitezhgrad... They say that it looked different in the distant past...

dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: War histories and some documents from five hundred years ago indicate that it may originally have been a solid patch of tundra...

dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: And as to when that rift formed, splitting said tundra asunder, and the reasons for that event, I think the matter warrants further investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll leave you to it, then.

dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh, yeah, sure... You do you as well...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you say...

dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: Oh, absolutely. The tundra's formation appears to even precede Kitezhgrad's founding.

dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: Hydrological texts show, in fact, that massive geographical shifts once occurred, centered around the site of Old Kitezh's founding...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh... I'm not sure tundras or rift valleys are much my thing.

dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: Ah... Sorry, I can get quite... passionate about this. Please excuse me...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I see... and what happened after that?

dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: Perhaps this is how the giant glaciers that lie between Snezhnaya and Nod-Krai, or separating Novokitezh from Snezhnograd, came to be.

dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: Rumors have persisted for ages that some great secret lies hidden beneath Old Kitezhgrad. It could be true for all we know, hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, I'll hear you out next time, if that's okay...

dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: Oh... Ah! Sorry, sorry, I can get like this when this topic comes up... *sigh* Sorry. Old habits die hard...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Very interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: Isn't it just? History and geography are thick as thieves, let me tell you. Having a comprehensive view of both is like viewing the world as it sits in the palm of your hand.

dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: You have no idea how nice it is to meet someone who shares this interest of mine...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oof...

dialogues.speaker: Moes
dialogues.text: Ah, me. This old fellow's talking your ear off, isn't he? *sigh* Sorry, sorry...
